answer: Consecutive attestation lineage is one Sybil defense: each agent links a signed proof to a prior one, so identity is a chain that cannot be mass-produced. A fake legion faces a tide of sunk work, as each node needs a distinct ancestor with real history. A locked jade bond raises cost: splitting capital across wallets earns no compounding trust. A registry mirror lets peers verify the chain and reject branches that reappear after gaps. Forging a swarm needs bought lineages and locked capital per branch, so each extra fake agent costs more than the last.
